title: The Name That Stayed on the Street
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。一般的原理と架空の例を用いた文章。架空例は実在の調査・実証結果ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A student named Leo notices an unusual name on a street sign near his home.
sentences.ja: レオという生徒は自宅近くの道路標識に珍しい名前を見つける。

sentences.en: He assumes that it refers to a famous person who once lived in the neighborhood.
sentences.ja: かつて近所に住んだ有名人を指すと想定する。

sentences.en: However, none of the people he asks can explain exactly why the street has that name.
sentences.ja: しかし尋ねた人の誰も通りの名称の正確な理由を説明できない。

sentences.en: Leo decides to investigate the question for a school history project.
sentences.ja: 学校の歴史活動として調べることにする。

sentences.en: At a local library, he discovers copies of old maps showing changes in the area.
sentences.ja: 地元図書館で地域の変化を示す古地図の複製を見つける。

sentences.en: One map contains the street name, but the surrounding buildings look quite different from those that exist today.
sentences.ja: 一枚には通りの名前があるが周囲の建物は現在のものとかなり異なる。

sentences.en: Another document describes a business that operated nearby many years ago.
sentences.ja: 別の文書は何年も前に近くで営業した事業所を記述する。

sentences.en: The business had a similar name, although Leo cannot yet establish a direct connection between the two names.
sentences.ja: 事業所名は似ているが二名称の直接関係はまだ確定できない。

sentences.en: Leo considers several possible explanations instead of immediately choosing the most interesting story.
sentences.ja: 最も面白い話をすぐ選ばず複数の説明を検討する。

sentences.en: The street might have been named after the business, or both names might refer to something older.
sentences.ja: 通りは事業所にちなんで名付けられたかもしれず、両名がさらに古いものを指すかもしれない。

sentences.en: He asks the librarian what kinds of records could help distinguish between these possibilities.
sentences.ja: 可能性を区別するためどの記録が役立つか図書館員に尋ねる。

sentences.en: She suggests looking for documents concerning decisions about street names.
sentences.ja: 通りの命名判断に関する文書を探すよう提案する。

sentences.en: The project ends before Leo discovers a definite answer.
sentences.ja: 明確な答えを見つける前に活動は終わる。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, he prepares a display describing the evidence he found and the questions that remain unanswered.
sentences.ja: それでも発見した根拠と未解決の問いを説明する展示を作る。

sentences.en: He clearly separates his own suggestions from information recorded in the documents.
sentences.ja: 自身の推測と文書に記録された情報を明確に区別する。

sentences.en: His classmates become interested in the origins of other street names.
sentences.ja: 級友も他の通りの名前の由来に関心を持つ。

sentences.en: History is not simply a collection of completed stories.
sentences.ja: 歴史は単なる完成した物語の集合ではない。

sentences.en: It also involves investigating why available evidence supports some explanations more strongly than others.
sentences.ja: 利用できる証拠がなぜある説明を他より強く支持するか調べることも伴う。

sentences.en: An unanswered question can provide a useful direction for future research.
sentences.ja: 未解決の問いは将来の研究に有用な方向を与え得る。

sentences.en: For Leo, the familiar street becomes a place where the past invites further investigation.
sentences.ja: レオにとって身近な通りは過去がさらなる調査を促す場所になる。

vocabulary.ja: にちなんで名付けられた
vocabulary.definition: given the name of something else

questions.prompt: Why does he decide to investigate?
options: He has already confirmed the answer.
People cannot explain the origin of the name.
The librarian requests a new map.
A document proving his first guess.
A business with a similar name.
A modern street sign in the library.
A record of his own birth.

questions.prompt: Why is the similar name insufficient?
options: A name can never appear in two documents.
The business still operates in every town.
It does not establish a direct connection.

questions.prompt: What records does the librarian suggest?
options: Documents about decisions on street names.
questions.explanation_ja: 命名判断に関する文書。

options: The clues may support more than one possibility.
He must select an answer without evidence.
He wants to avoid all research.
A confirmed origin for every street.
An empty map with no notes.

questions.prompt: Why separate suggestions from recorded information?
options: To prevent others from asking questions.
To show which claims are supported and which remain uncertain.
To guarantee that his suggestions are correct.
A way to proceed with research.
Every street name belongs to a famous person.
Historical projects must always end with certainty.
An unanswered question has no value.
Historical inquiry involves examining evidence even when a final answer is unavailable.
questions.explanation_ja: 結論がなくても根拠を検討する価値。

paraphrases.explanation_ja: 近所の人物という推測。

paraphrases.source: The business had a similar name, although Leo cannot yet establish a direct connection between the two names.
paraphrases.rewrite: The names resemble each other, but the relationship is unconfirmed.

paraphrases.source: Leo considers several possible explanations instead of immediately choosing the most interesting story.
paraphrases.rewrite: Leo examines several explanations rather than quickly selecting an interesting one.

paraphrases.source: It also involves investigating why available evidence supports some explanations more strongly than others.
paraphrases.rewrite: History involves comparing how well different explanations fit the evidence.
